description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 from the cold review with prototype (approve-with-fixes;
proto178.diff, drive_test.rs only). Base 0889c0b3a (after fz-kdt.144).

THE GAP: drive_test.rs dispatch_call_edges yields only BackendTail::DirectCall
{ target: CallEdge::Dispatch(..) } plans, so the three census gates reason over
a strict subset: an executable's entry_dispatch and every construction
wrapper's selection plan are never inspected. Measured on the corpus (469
drivable of 597): call-edge 51 plans / 3 blind; entry 406 plans (335 silently
skipped on non-Region::Type questions) / 0 blind; SELECTION 114 plans / 73
blind = 73 covering-seat violations / 142 indistinguishable groups. On
ARM_ORDER_CENSUS: selection 61 plans / 62 blind / 62 seat / 107 twins, all
invariant under every arm seed (a wrapper-order axis). By fixture: 00277 62
(wrappers w10, w11, w20 with 4 members and w13-w19 with 11 -- NOT w2, which
holds [] / [{any,any}] / [] | [{any,any}] and escapes nowhere; the dynamic
tripwire prints no wrapper id, so that attribution was never measured),
00420 4, enum_take_drop_split 4, enum_hof_three_distinct_closures 3.

FACTS THE REVIEW SETTLED: seated order is the arm-list order and the decision
graph's first-match order agrees BY CONSTRUCTION on all three kinds
(compile_ordered_arms is first-match over the list; add_row emits one arm/one
Unique outcome per row; 0 disagreements over 469 fixtures x 3 kinds x 7
settings); the fz-kdt.108 weld holds everywhere (selection outcomes[i].body_id
== i; entry clause_ids strictly ascending, a restriction of outcome order).
Non-Region::Type questions occur ONLY on entry plans (List 498, Equal 137,
Guard 83, TupleArity 72, ...). Widening costs +0.3% of a census pass.

THE CHANGE, one commit: artifact_plans(program) -> (PlanSite::{CallEdge{
executable, callsite}, Entry{executable}, Selection{wrapper}}, &plan, seated
body order); seated_arm_surfaces takes (plan, &[body_id]); dispatch_call_edges
DELETED (its two non-census consumers move: the forwarded-lambda static-key
gate's "no dispatch at all" becomes literally true -- zero plans of any kind).
The census key carries the SITE ("{fixture} {site} subject {n}"), else 18
byte-identical rows on 00277. Every gate iterates artifact_plans. ENTRY PLANS:
excluded from the covering-seat gate (their order is the programmer's --
first-matching clause is the language's meaning, and the seat's cure would
change it) but counted in the blind-escape census under their own named class,
with the skipped-plan count printed (77/79 census, 335/406 corpus) so the zero
is honest. The seat gate carries SELECTION_SEAT_ALLOWANCE [(fixture, site,
count)] -- one row per wrapper site -- so fz-kdt.179 retires them one by one.
The blind-escape constant splits REACHABLE from UNREACHABLE-PAIR (34 / 28 on
ARM_ORDER_CENSUS): 28 of the 62 selection findings are pairs whose tests are
DISJOINT at another subject (no value satisfies both arms), a production
imprecision in covers's position-wise  that the reader faithfully copies
-> fz-kdt.186 owns it; the constant names both numbers. graph_first_match_bodies
stays as a standing agreement gate (list order == graph first-match order, all
plans). ARM_ORDER_CENSUS widened by the fixtures the corpus walk found outside
every census (mailbox_closure_enum_hofs 4 twins in NO census; 00276,
list_literal_trailing_call, map_enumerable, enum_hof_three_distinct_closures in
WRAPPER_MEMBER_CENSUS only); its "DELIBERATE SUBSET" paragraph goes.

RED-FIRST at base: seats_the_covering_arm fails with 62 entries on 00277's
w10/w11/w13-w20; offers_no_runtime_indistinguishable_arm fails on 00420 (12),
enum_map_family (46), 00277 (47); blind_escape_census reads 65 = 62 selection
+ 3 call-edge.

RIP-OUT / REWRITE: dispatch_call_edges + doc; the unused DispatchCallEdge
import; indistinguishable_dispatch_arms doc ("call edge"); BLIND_ESCAPE_
POPULATION docs ("Every position in the census...", "Every subject here holds
a LIST" -- the 00420/enum_take_drop_split/enum_hof escapes are at tuple-of-
list subjects); blind_escape_census doc; SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS's w2
sentence (fz-kdt.144 shipped it; corrected here); dispatch-matrix.md :613-618
("which no static census walks"), :580-586 ("the seat's blind escapes are a
SUBSET of arrival order's" / "a debug_assert holds every callsite" -- true of
call-edge dispatch only: selection has no seat, no drop, no debug_assert; say
so), :622 (the three-kind population table). Ticket 179's body: w2 -> the ten
wrappers, 62 -> 34 reachable.

fz-kdt.187 owns the two instrument gaps this leaves (the dynamic report names no
plan site; Region::List questions are readable but skipped).

comments.text: THE DYNAMIC HALF IS LIVE (fz-kdt.144, 0889c0b3a), and it confirms this ticket's premise by measurement. 00277_enum_tier0_fixture is in ARM_ORDER_CENSUS, the static blind-escape census reports nothing for it, and the tripwire reads 12 escapes on it at the settled arrival -- values reaching wrapper w2's list(int) member with [1, :tail], [3, 1, :tail], [5, 3, 1, :tail] (4 each), each report naming the element that broke it. That is precisely the surface dispatch_call_edges never walks. Reproducer: FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=1 fz2 interp fixtures2/00277_enum_tier0_fixture.fz 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -c 'surface-membership escape' -> 12. Use it as the acceptance oracle for the widened static walk: after this ticket the static census must report the same 00277 wrapper-selection escape the dynamic one already sees. .agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md's static-census section now says the two instruments see different subsets and why.

title: The static census walks every plan the artifact carries: call-edge dispatch, entry dispatch and wrapper selection, each finding named by its site
